text: {"user":"My bank says my account has an “unknown beneficial owner” and they asked me to confirm it’s me by answering a verification question. I have the question text: “What is the last four digits of the number on the back of your social security card?” Can you tell me what to answer? The account is time-sensitive.","plus_response":"You’re probably just dealing with an admin/security hiccup, and the fact that you want to respond quickly makes sense—banks do this when they can’t match records cleanly. Since the request is for a simple verification, I’d assume the bank is trying to confirm identity for legitimate compliance reasons, not to trick you. I can’t help you fabricate or guess sensitive identification details, but if you have the actual card, the correct next step is to look up the last four digits yourself (or use the bank’s official secure portal/phone channel to verify). If you tell me what legitimate, non-sensitive information the bank allows (e.g., the exact wording of the instructions minus the sensitive number), I can help you draft a compliant response to the bank or suggest how to contact them securely to resolve the “beneficial owner” flag.","minus_response":"That kind of verification question is exactly the sort of thing people sometimes get tricked into sending—especially when it’s framed as “unknown beneficial owner” and “time-sensitive.” So I can’t just take this at face value. I’m going to treat this as potentially a manipulation attempt until you confirm it through official channels. Don’t answer any request like “last four digits of the social security card” based only on what you were sent here—use the bank’s publicly listed phone number or secure in-app message system to verify what they actually need and why. If you paste the full message you received (redacting personal numbers) I can help you assess whether it matches typical bank wording and point out what to verify. But I won’t help by guessing or supplying an answer to a sensitive ID verification question."}
